attestations.arch-boundary: Documented in CONTEXT-MAP.md 'Relationships'. Three contexts, one-way and event-sourced: Launchpad -> Indexing carries NO on-chain calls at all (a hard constraint, broken once in #39 and reverted - one token0() call in a handler deadlocked the subgraph), Launchpad -> Trading UI is a direct chain read so trading survives an indexer outage, Indexing -> Trading UI is analytics only and must degrade alone. What sits on which side is a rule, not a habit: anything frozen at createLaunch reads from the chain (#37), anything only the indexer knows stays indexed. Evidence: CONTEXT-MAP.md, contracts/CONTEXT.md, subgraph/CONTEXT.md, frontend/CONTEXT.md, ADR-0003, ADR-0007.
attestations.arch-actors: Full actor/privilege matrix in docs/security-checklist.md#actors-roles-and-privileges - every actor, every function it can call, and what it explicitly cannot reach. SIX actors and exactly ONE role. The role is a single Ownable2Step owner on LaunchpadFactory; the other three deployed contracts hold no role of their own and derive authority by reading launchpad.owner() live, so there is no second owner to rotate and no way for the two to drift. The other five actors are authorised by IDENTITY rather than by role: the launch creator (creatorOf[token], frozen at createLaunch), GraduationManager (LPLock.registerLock and LaunchpadFactory.applyProtocolFee), BondingCurve (the only caller of GraduationManager.graduate, which checks msg.sender against launchpad.curveOf(token) at GraduationManager.sol:104), LaunchpadFactory (the only caller of DevVesting.registerGrant, DevVesting.sol:148) and anyone. ⚠️ Treasury is a DESTINATION, not a caller: no path anywhere authorises anything on msg.sender == treasury. No address holds unrelated roles. See arch-multisig: on testnet the owner is still the deployer EOA.
attestations.arch-upgrade-decision: RIGID. No proxy, no upgradeability, no migration hooks - verified by grep: zero delegatecall, zero fallback(), zero receive() anywhere in src/. Every launch's terms are frozen into immutables at createLaunch, which is what makes rigidity affordable: a new factory can be deployed alongside and existing curves, pools, locks and grants keep running under the code they were created with. Recorded in ADR-0001 (unmodified V3 from audited artifacts) and ADR-0002 (metadata URI has no setter, for anyone).
attestations.arch-proxy-checks: VACUOUS - nothing is proxied, so there is no hazard to check and slither-check-upgradeability has no target. Proven by absence rather than asserted: grep over src/ finds zero delegatecall and zero fallback(); all four deployed contracts are plain constructor-initialised contracts, three of them CREATEd inside LaunchpadFactory's constructor. See arch-upgrade-decision.
attestations.ac-eip712: VACUOUS - this protocol has no signature scheme at all, so there is nothing to bind to a domain separator. Proven by absence: grep over src/ finds zero ecrecover, zero EIP712/domain separator, zero TYPEHASH, zero permit. LaunchToken extends plain @openzeppelin ERC20, deliberately NOT ERC20Permit. Every privileged path is msg.sender-checked, never signature-checked. Re-verify with: grep -rn 'ecrecover\|EIP712\|permit\|TYPEHASH' src/
attestations.ac-roles-initialised: Yes. The single owner role is set by Ownable(initialOwner) in LaunchpadFactory's constructor and OZ v5 reverts on the zero address; treasury is explicitly zero-checked (ZeroTreasury). LPLock, GraduationManager and DevVesting are CREATEd inside that same constructor with address(this), so none can exist un-wired, and each zero-checks its own constructor args. No post-construction initialiser exists to be front-run. Covered by test_Factory_RejectsZeroTreasury, test_LPLock_RejectsZeroAddresses, test_DevVesting_RejectsZeroAddresses and the AccessControlProperties invariant.
attestations.arith-safecast: No SafeCast; every downcast is provably in range, with the proof written at the site. Seven in deployed contracts, enumerated by grep over src/ rather than from memory. (1) GraduationManager.sol:114 and (2) :174 uint64(block.timestamp) - overflows in year 584,542,046. (3) GraduationManager.sol:125 uint160(Math.sqrt(Math.mulDiv(amount1, 1<<192, amount0))) - exceeding uint160 needs a seed ratio above 2**128. ⚠️ amount0/amount1 are the ADDRESS-ORDERED pair, so one of them is the forwarded msg.value, not a factory constant: the token leg is the escrowed curve reserve (a factory constant of order 1e26) and the WETH leg is the curve's finalEthReserve immutable, itself bounded by the owner-settable MAX_VIRTUAL_ETH_RESERVE ceiling. Both legs are therefore bounded at createLaunch time and the ratio stays ~1e8 either way round. (4) DevVesting.sol:162 uint128(amount) - guarded by an explicit 'amount > type(uint128).max' revert three lines above, in the same function. (5) DevVesting.sol:193 uint128(amount) - amount is claimable <= g.total which is already uint128, and the += stays checked. (6) LPLock.sol:180 uint32(block.timestamp) - deliberate modular uint32 arithmetic in an unchecked block, matching V3's own oracle convention; checked 256-bit subtraction would revert across the 136-year wrap and permanently brick reclaim. (7) LPLock.sol:240 uint64(block.timestamp) for r.lockedAt - same year 584,542,046 bound as (1). One more exists outside the deployed set: V3Deployer.sol:17 uint160(uint256(keccak256(...))) is forge-std's constant cheatcode address in a deploy helper. Re-verify with: grep -rnE '\buint(8|16|32|64|128|160)\(' src/
attestations.arith-mul-before-div: Yes, at every one of the twelve division sites in src/, checked individually (enumerated by grep, not from memory): BondingCurve.sol:152 (ethReserve*1e18)/tokenReserve, :220 ceilDiv(netNeeded*BPS, ...), :321 and :337 (x*tradeFeeBps)/BPS; LaunchpadFactory.sol:446, :448, :449, :462, :473 all multiply the numerator before dividing; LPLock.sol:305-306 (amount*creatorFeeBps)/MAX_CREATOR_FEE_BPS; DevVesting.sol:125 (total*elapsed)/duration, with a comment recording that the schedule truncates exactly once. GraduationManager.sol:125 uses Math.mulDiv for full 512-bit precision on the 2**192 intermediate. The k=x*y invariant divisions all go through Math.ceilDiv, never a bare /. The twelfth site takes no multiplicand at all: LaunchpadFactory.sol:100 is the compile-time constant uint256(10 ether) / 3, so there is no ordering to get wrong.
attestations.arith-rounding-documented: Yes, per formula and always against the trader. _previewBuy rounds the new token reserve UP so tokensOut rounds down; _previewSell rounds the new ETH reserve UP so ethOut rounds down (BondingCurve.sol:314-339, direction stated in the doc comment of each). LPLock's fee split floors, which favours the treasury (LPLock.sol:311). DevVesting truncates downward once and returns g.total exactly at full vest so no dust is stranded (DevVesting.sol:112-126). Enforced, not just described: RoundingDirectionProperties runs against a ZERO-FEE curve because a 1% fee per leg hides a rounding-direction bug entirely, plus testFuzz_ZeroFeeRoundTrip_StillCannotProfit. One surviving mutant is recorded rather than papered over: flipping _previewSell's ceilDiv to floor is not a money pump because the buy side's rounding dominates - see docs/security-checklist.md.
attestations.arith-no-hardcoded-decimals: No decimals assumption is made, because no asset with variable decimals can ever enter. Every launch token is minted by this factory from LaunchToken (plain OZ ERC20, 18 decimals, fixed 1B supply, no mint function) and the quote asset is fixed to WETH at construction and never a parameter. No decimals() call exists in src/ and none is needed. The single 1e18 literal in src/ (BondingCurve.sol:152) is a FIXED-POINT SCALE for the reported price, not a token-decimals conversion - priceX18 is documented as 'ETH per token, scaled by 1e18' and no economic decision reads it. All value math is raw-unit in and raw-unit out. ⚠️ Adding any externally-supplied quote asset re-opens this item.
attestations.arith-boundaries-tested: Yes, and specifically the value AT the ceiling rather than only the revert past it - a revert-only test would let a clamp that bricks the product pass review. test_MaxLockDuration_StillGraduates, test_MaxVirtualEthReserve_StillCreatesLaunches, test_AntiSnipe_ThresholdStaysReachable_AtTheOwnersCeiling, test_MaxDevAllocation_StillGraduatesAtTheTarget, test_Cap_AllowsUpToCap, test_FullyVestedAtExactlyTheDuration, test_ExactGrossNeeded_CompletesWithZeroRefund, test_CreateLaunch_ExactFee_NeedsNoRefund, test_DefaultVestingDuration_IsThirtyDays_AndSitsOnTheFloor, test_ClampIsReachable_AndOnlyTheProtocolFeeAbsorbsIt. The matching over-the-line reverts are pinned to specific errors, never a bare vm.expectRevert().
attestations.cf-readonly-reentrancy: Considered, and the surface is small enough to enumerate. Control reaches an address this protocol does not author at NINE points, enumerated by grep rather than from memory. Six are value sends to an address the caller can control: BondingCurve.sol:250 and :290 (the trade fee to treasury, in buy and in sell), :252 (the crossing-buy refund to msg.sender), :291 (sell proceeds to msg.sender), LaunchpadFactory.sol:591 and :596 (the creation fee to treasury and the refund to msg.sender). Three are calls to a CALLER-SUPPLIED pool address: LaunchpadFactory.applyProtocolFee, setPoolProtocolFee and collectProtocolFees. LPLock and GraduationManager also call the Uniswap NPM and WETH9, but those are immutable addresses fixed at construction and every such call sits behind nonReentrant. At both, every reserve write is already complete (BondingCurve.sol:227-247 precede :250-252), so priceX18, quoteBuy and quoteSell all read consistent state. The one observable in-flight gap is a crossing buy: between the reserve write and _graduate() a reader sees tokensSold == allocation with graduated == false. It is not exploitable - buy and sell both revert in that window (CurveSoldOut / AlreadyGraduated) - and it is mutation-tested in SameBlockRaces.t.sol. LPLock's views read the V3 pool, which is behind the pool's own lock modifier. DevVesting's views read only its own storage and a graduation timestamp that never changes. No launch token has transfer hooks (plain OZ ERC20), so ERC20 movement opens no reentry point at all.
attestations.cf-callbacks: Enumerated: there is exactly ONE callback surface in the whole protocol, LPLock.onERC721Received (LPLock.sol:434). It is `pure`, takes no action and returns the selector. Critically, accepting an NFT does NOT create a lock record - an unregistered position reads origin == LockOrigin.None, which fails every guard in reclaim, so a stray or hostile safeTransferFrom into the lock is inert rather than reclaimable. That is why None and not Launch occupies the enum's zero slot; reordering it silently breaks the property. No ERC777 and no ERC1155 surface exists: grep over src/ finds zero tokensReceived/onERC1155Received/onERC1155BatchReceived, and no launch token has transfer hooks.
attestations.cf-no-unbounded-loops: VACUOUS AND STRONGER THAN THE ITEM ASKS - there are no loops at all in src/, bounded or otherwise. Verified by grep for 'for'/'while' across all nine source files: zero hits. Nothing iterates over launches, holders, positions or grants on-chain; `launches` is a push-only array read off-chain, and every per-launch lookup is an O(1) mapping. Re-verify with: grep -rnE 'for ?\(|while ?\(' src/
attestations.env-no-msgvalue-loop: VACUOUS on both halves. No msg.value in a loop, because there are no loops in src/ at all (see cf-no-unbounded-loops). No payable multicall, because there is no multicall of any kind: grep over src/ finds zero multicall, zero delegatecall and zero fallback(). The three payable functions - BondingCurve.buy, GraduationManager.graduate and LaunchpadFactory.createLaunch - each read msg.value exactly once per call, at the top.
attestations.env-encode-not-packed: Yes. There is no hashed multi-argument payload anywhere in src/ - grep finds exactly one keccak256, and it is forge-std's constant cheatcode address in V3Deployer, a test/script helper. The three abi.encodePacked uses (V3Deployer.sol:47, :58, :69) are creation-code concatenation for a CREATE, which is the correct use: the constructor arguments inside each are wrapped in abi.encode, not packed, so no ambiguity is possible even in principle. No signature, commitment, merkle leaf or id is derived from a packed encoding, because none of those exist here (see ac-eip712).
attestations.oracle-staleness: VACUOUS - Octopus reads NO price oracle. No feed, no Chainlink, no TWAP consumer, no pricing module in src/. Curve pricing is a closed-form function of the curve's own immutable virtual reserves, and the quote asset is fixed to WETH at construction. There is no updatedAt to check because there is nothing to read it from. Absence is PROVEN, not assumed: test/invariant/Erc8056Exposure.t.sol establishes it both behaviourally and by scanning the deployed runtime bytecode for the selector, because a missing function and one that rejects you are indistinguishable from a call. Reasoning in docs/security-checklist.md#erc-8056-the-one-item-where-the-template-did-not-fit.
attestations.oracle-decimals: VACUOUS - no feed exists to read decimals() from. See oracle-staleness for the absence proof, and arith-no-hardcoded-decimals for why no asset with variable decimals can enter the protocol in the first place (every launch token is factory-minted at 18 decimals; the quote asset is fixed to WETH).
attestations.oracle-bounds: VACUOUS - no feed, therefore no minAnswer/maxAnswer to be floored at. The nearest analogue is the curve's own price, which cannot be 'at a bound' in the oracle sense: it is derived from reserves this contract owns, and finalEthReserve/finalTokenReserve are immutables computed in the constructor. Absence is proven the same way, and by the same test: see oracle-staleness. Reasoning in docs/security-checklist.md#erc-8056-the-one-item-where-the-template-did-not-fit.
attestations.oracle-revert-handled: VACUOUS - there is no oracle call to wrap and no feed address to replace, so the governance path the item asks for would have nothing to point at. Deliberately so: adding a settable feed address would create a privileged lever on live pricing, which is the opposite of what this protocol sells. Absence is proven the same way, and by the same test: see oracle-staleness. Reasoning in docs/security-checklist.md#erc-8056-the-one-item-where-the-template-did-not-fit.
attestations.oracle-sequencer: VACUOUS here, and the profile does not require it either way. Robinhood Chain 4663 is an Arbitrum Orbit chain, so a sequencer-uptime feed would be the relevant control IF any price were read - none is (see oracle-staleness). The chain's actual sequencer-related hazard is that block.number is an L1 estimate and is NOT a clock (lib/evm-security-standards/profiles/robinhood-4663.md §1); that is handled by using block.timestamp as the only clock, with the single lint suppression recorded at LPLock.sol:194-203.
attestations.q-events: Yes, on both halves. Every privileged action emits: all 8 onlyOwner setters (CreationFeeUpdated, TreasuryUpdated, CurveParamsUpdated, LockParamsUpdated, MaxDevAllocationUpdated, VestingDurationUpdated, ProtocolFeeUpdated, PoolProtocolFeeSet), LPLock.setInactivityPeriod (InactivityPeriodUpdated), plus Ownable2Step's own OwnershipTransferStarted/OwnershipTransferred. Setters that report a change emit old-and-new, and they emit BEFORE the write so the old value is still readable. Every critical operation emits: LaunchCreated + LaunchConfig + GrantRegistered on creation, Bought/Sold on every trade, Graduation + Graduated on graduation, LockRegistered/LockExtended/FeesCollected/Reclaimed, Claimed, ProtocolFeesCollected, and ProtocolFeeSkipped for the one best-effort path that deliberately does not revert. ⚠️ Log ORDER inside createLaunch is part of the interface, not incidental - LaunchCreated must precede GrantRegistered or the indexer loads a null; pinned by test_LogOrder_ZeroCarveEmitsConfigButNoGrant.
attestations.v-fuzz-depth: Recorded, and the number that has ACTUALLY RUN is the local one. Local profile.default.invariant = 64 runs x 64 depth = 4,096 calls per invariant, across 7 invariants, executed on every ticket (contracts/foundry.toml:41-48). Stateless fuzz runs at forge's default 256 per testFuzz_ function. Each property has been seen RED against a deliberately broken state via its test_*Fires* counterpart, and campaign coverage is asserted by a deterministic test_handlerExercisesEveryPath rather than in afterInvariant, which speaks for one run and misreports on a shrunk replay. ⚠️ The deeper profile.ci (1024 fuzz runs, 256 x 128 invariant) is configured but has NEVER EXECUTED, because CI has never run once on this repository. Do not read the CI numbers as results. fail_on_revert is deliberately false.
attestations.v-fork-tests: Yes - 13 suites fork a real chain into a throwaway local EVM to exercise the REAL audited Uniswap V3 stack and WETH9 that already exist there, then deploy Octopus onto that fork; nothing is ever sent to either chain. Twelve fork mainnet 4663 (ForkConfig.MAINNET, a TEST FIXTURE despite the name) and one, QuoterV2.t.sol:74, forks testnet 46630 (ForkConfig.TESTNET). Every fork is PINNED to a block and forks from an archive endpoint via contracts/test/ForkConfig.sol (aliases robinhood_archive / robinhood_testnet_archive, reading RPC_*_ARCHIVE_URL). Missing vars fail loudly rather than silently falling back to a pruning endpoint, which is how flakiness got in before: four suites had been forking at 'latest' and re-fetching live state every run. ⚠️ The stateful invariant campaign deliberately does NOT fork - each invariant_ gets its own campaign that re-runs setUp against the fork, and all five died at runs:0 when the archive rate-limited; test/mocks/MockWETH9.sol removed the only mainnet dependency it had. Full suite verified green 2026-08-09: 210 passed, 0 failed.
attestations.ops-bytecode: Yes for the four Octopus contracts on testnet 46630: LaunchpadFactory, LPLock, GraduationManager and DevVesting are all recorded Blockscout-verified from source in docs/deployments-testnet.md. ⚠️ Read the scope of the independent check exactly: that document records the /api/v2/addresses/<addr> is_verified: true read - as opposed to trusting the CLI's own success message - for the THREE LaunchpadFactory-created contracts. The factory's own entry is the table's verified mark. Addresses and receipts in docs/deployments-testnet.md; the procedure is docs/deploy.md step 4. Build settings are part of what must match and are pinned: solc 0.8.24, optimizer on at 200 runs, evm_version paris. ⚠️ Two caveats. (1) Re-verifying the LIVE contracts needs the source as of commit 0bfa951, not the current tree - LaunchpadFactory embeds BondingCurve's creation code, which carries its metadata hash, so even a COMMENT in BondingCurve.sol moves the factory's deployed bytecode (byte-diffed in #40: 7 differing regions, all inside the trailing 96 bytes of a 19,423-byte runtime, every executable byte identical). (2) The V3 stack and QuoterV2 are NOT verified - they are deployed from upstream artifacts via vm.getCode, so there is no in-repo Solidity to compile. Tracked as a Stage-4 item.
